questions.q: What does vertical scaling fix, and what is its hard ceiling?
options: It adds more CPU, RAM, or disk speed to an existing node with no architectural change, but there's a maximum instance size and it doesn't help once disk I/O is saturated
It scales write throughput indefinitely with no ceiling
It only works on sharded clusters, never on a single node
It automatically distributes data across multiple shards
questions.explain: Vertical scaling is the simplest lever but has a real upper limit and doesn't solve disk I/O-saturated write bottlenecks.

questions.q: Why doesn't adding more replica set secondaries help with write throughput?
options: Every write still goes to the single primary, regardless of how many secondaries exist
Secondaries actually slow down writes further
Replica sets have no primary at all
Adding secondaries removes the primary from the cluster
questions.explain: Secondaries can serve reads but all writes route through the primary — replicas scale read capacity only.

questions.q: According to this lesson's capacity planning framework, when should sharding be the chosen strategy?
options: Only once write throughput or data volume has genuinely outgrown what a single primary and vertical scaling/replicas can handle
As the very first option whenever any performance issue appears
Only for read-heavy workloads
Sharding should never be used in production
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns that reaching for sharding first, before other options are exhausted, is a common and costly mistake.

questions.q: What real consistency tradeoff comes with reading from replica set secondaries?
options: Reads from secondaries can return slightly stale data under replication lag
Secondaries always return more current data than the primary
There is no tradeoff at all
Secondaries can never be read from under any configuration
questions.explain: Replication lag means secondary reads aren't guaranteed to reflect the very latest writes — a real, not free, tradeoff.

questions.q: What is 'working set' in the context of vertical scaling decisions?
options: The portion of data and indexes MongoDB needs cached in RAM for good performance
The total disk space used by all MongoDB backups
The number of active replica set members
The set of shard keys currently in use
questions.explain: Insufficient working-set memory is one of the real problems vertical scaling (more RAM) genuinely solves.
